status: DRAFT v0.1: not yet reviewed, pretested or calibrated.
notes: Two possible sub-dimensions: funding/choice and curriculum/parental control. High pole is consistently 'more choice and parental control / less public provision'.

items.stem: Should public money follow students to the school their family chooses, including private schools?
options: No; fund public schools only
Only to public charter schools, not private schools
Yes, including private schools, for low-income families
Yes, including private schools, for every family

items.stem: How many public charter schools should there be?
items.scope: Charter schools are tuition-free public schools run independently of the school district.
options: Fewer; limit or close them
About as many as today
More
Many more; let any qualified group open one

items.stem: Who should have the most say over what public schools teach?
options: Teachers and education experts
State education boards
Local elected school boards
Parents, with the right to review all materials

items.stem: Should parents be able to take their children out of lessons they object to?
options: No; the curriculum is for all students
Only for sex education
Yes, for any lesson that conflicts with their values

items.stem: Should public schools teach about gender identity?
items.scope: For example, that some people identify as a gender different from their sex at birth.
options: Yes, starting in elementary school
Only in middle and high school
Only in high school, with parents choosing whether their child takes part
No, at any grade

items.stem: What kind of sex education should public high schools teach?
items.scope: Required health classes, with parents able to opt out.
options: Full coverage, including contraception, consent and sexual orientation
Contraception and consent, while encouraging teens to wait
Abstinence only
None; leave it to parents

items.stem: What should happen to existing federal student loan debt?
items.scope: Loans from the federal government, not private lenders.
options: Cancel all of it
Cancel up to about $10,000 to $20,000 per borrower
Cancel only for people misled by their schools, or after years of public service
No cancellation

items.stem: Should monthly federal student loan payments be capped at a share of the borrower's income?
options: Yes, at 5% of income or less, with any remaining debt forgiven after 10 years
Yes, at about 10% of income, with remaining debt forgiven after 20 to 25 years
No; borrowers should repay what they borrowed on standard terms

items.stem: Should tuition be free at public colleges and universities?
options: Yes, for everyone
Yes, for families earning under about $125,000
Only community college
No

items.stem: What should happen to the federal Department of Education?
items.scope: Its main jobs are student aid, civil rights enforcement and funding for low-income schools.
options: Expand it and increase federal school funding
Keep it about as it is
Shrink it and send money and control to states
Close it

items.stem: How should schools handle students who are repeatedly disruptive or violent?
options: Counseling and repairing harm; suspend only as a last resort
A mix of counseling and suspension
Suspend or expel them to protect other students

items.subtopic: Merit-based admissions to selective public schools
items.stem: How should selective public high schools choose their students?
items.scope: Public schools with more applicants than seats, such as specialized science schools.
options: A lottery among qualified applicants
Grades and tests, plus seats for the top students from every middle school
Admission test and grades only
